rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾānic recitation has three tempos: tahqīq is very slow, tedvīr moderate, and hadr fast, measured by the length of elongation.
rows.anchor: Kur’an kıraati üç mertebe üzere tasnif olunmuştur: Tahkik, tedvir, hadr.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author assigns ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and Warsh from Nāfiʿ to tahqīq; Ibn ʿĀmir and Kisāʾī to tedvīr; the rest to hadr, while every mode must preserve each letter and vowel fully.
rows.anchor: Âsım, Hamza, Nâfi‘den Verş kıraatleri tahkik, İbn Âmir, Kisâî kıraatleri tedvir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All recitation modes require tartīl in its essential sense; the later command to recite what is easy permits the faster tempos.
rows.anchor: asıl mânasıyla tertil hepsinde şarttır. Böyle hadr ve tedvir taksîmine cevaz veren ise gelecek olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first purpose of rising at night is measured Qurʾānic recitation; although it also covers teaching and recitation beyond prayer, rising in this context ordinarily means prayer.
rows.anchor: burada tertîl-i Kur’an emri kıyamdan ilk maksad bu olduğunu gösterir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because little Qurʾān had yet been revealed, prolonged nightly recitation trained the Prophet for worship and application, rather than serving merely as memorization.
rows.anchor: henüz çok bir şey nâzil olmadığı cihetle her gece bu kadar uzun müddet kalkıp da Kur’an tertil etmek bunun mücerred bellemek için değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavy utterance is the Qurʾān and the mission: revelation imposes difficult commands, responsibility, and obligations that cannot be rejected and must be enacted.
rows.anchor: tahammülü, icrâ ve îfâsı çok zor olan büyük bir kelâmı üzerine indirip tatbik ve icrâsını sana emredeceğiz

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that revelation came so intensely that on a very cold day sweat poured from the Prophet’s brow as it lifted.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Hazret-i Âişe demişti ki: “Gayet soğuk bir günde vahiy inerken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At ʿArafāt during the Farewell Pilgrimage, revelation’s weight nearly made the Prophet’s camel al-ʿAḍbāʾ collapse.
rows.anchor: nâm devesinin üzerinde iken vahiy gelince ağırlıktan deve çökekalmıştı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is easy to recite but difficult to practice; its reward also weighs heavily on the Scale.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ı okumak kolay olsa da onunla amel zordur. Sonra, Mîzan’da ecr ü sevâbı da ağırdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night prayer and measured recitation are preparatory spiritual discipline, strengthening the self to carry out the harder commands that follow.
rows.anchor: gece kıyamı ve Kur’an tertîli ile emir, o cümleden olmak üzere gelecek olan ağır emirlerin icrâsına kābiliyet ve isti‘dad kesbetmek üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase nāshiʾat al-layl can mean the self formed at night, an event occurring at night, or the night’s own awakening and emergence.
rows.anchor: gece nâşi’esi; gece yetişen nefis, veya gece vukū‘a gelen hâdise veya gece neş’esi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waṭʾ can mean pressing, treading, softening, preparing, making something fitting, or a low place between rises; Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with a different vowel and elongation, evoking concord.
rows.anchor: Ebû Amr ve İbn Âmir kıraatlerinde vâv’ın kesri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night vigil is more forceful, intimate, or attuned to heart and conscience: quiet removes daytime distractions, opens perception, and better protects sincerity from display and social pressure.
rows.anchor: Gece sükûnet ve inkıtâ‘hengâmı olduğu için uyanık olanların gözü gönlüne daha mutabık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night speech is sounder because quiet supports recitation, reflection, study, recollection, and better listening.
rows.anchor: gürültüler kesilmiş bulunacağı cihetle kıraat ve tefekkür, mütalaa ve tezekkür,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of the long daytime activity is that worldly movement and duties obstruct the quiet and concentration available at night.
rows.anchor: Yeryüzünde hareket, meşgul edecek, kıraat ve ibadete mâni‘işler vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading is that daytime is a suitable time to attend to other needs and important tasks.
rows.anchor: diğer havâyicini ve mühim işlerini görecek müsâid bir zaman vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third, future-oriented reading offers glad tidings that after the commanded night vigil the Prophet will attain a long period of purification; the author compares the dawn image with 74:34.
rows.anchor: Bu kıyam ile me’mur olduğun gecenin bir gündüzü gelecektir ki sen o zaman uzun bir nezâhete ve temizliğe ereceksin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering the Lord includes glorification, takbīr, praise, affirmation of unity, prayer, Qurʾān recitation, teaching, exhortation, and guidance throughout night and day.
rows.anchor: tesbih ve tehlil, tekbir, temcid, tevhid, namaz, Kur’an okumak, ilim tâlimi, Allah için nasihat ve irşad

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabattul means withdrawing from other concerns and turning wholly to God in sincere obedience, without letting worldly pursuits occupy the heart.
rows.anchor: kendini her şeyden çekerek Rabbine çekil, ihlâs ile O’nun emr ü tâatine meşgul ol

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabattul literally involves cutting oneself off; Maryam was called Batūl for devotion, and a woman uninterested in men could also be called Batūl.
rows.anchor: ibadette Allah’a inkıtâ‘ından dolayı Hazret-i Meryem’e “Betûl” denilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī explains the wording as naming the ultimate goal, tabattul, before its necessary means, tabtīl: one must first sever worldly attachments to attain devotion to God.
rows.anchor: Evvelâ, maksûdun bizzat olan tebettülü sonra da onun şartı olan tebtîli zikreylemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching remembrance and devotion to the name Rabb directs attention from creatures to the Creator’s governance of inward and outward affairs, and teaches surrender from action to its agent and judgment to its judge.
rows.anchor: Hâlık teâlâ’nın ahkâm-ı rubûbiyetine, enfüsî ve âfâkī tedbir ve tasarrufu esrârını mülâhazaya dalmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb of east and west means Lord of all worlds: whatever rises or sets is His, and He alone manages, nurtures, and owns every matter.
rows.anchor: bütün maşrık ve mağribin Rabbidir Rabbü’l-âlemîn’dir. Âlemde gerek parlayan gerek sönen her şeyin her hususta rabbi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone is deity, He alone deserves complete love, worship, and obedience; hoping in anyone else is futile because both lordship and divinity are His.
rows.anchor: Kemâl-i mahabbet ile sevilip gönül verilecek ve ibadet edilecek, emrine teslim olunacak O’ndan başka mâbud yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking God as wakīl means entrusting all affairs to Him and following His command rather than one’s own wishes or other people’s desires; His power can set affairs right and defeat opponents.
rows.anchor: O’na dayan, ne senin kendinin ne de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People’s dealings with God are more important than dealings with others; in the latter, patiently leave opponents alone for now.
rows.anchor: Evvelki kısım daha mühim olduğu için sûrenin evvelinden buraya kadar ona müte‘allik olan esaslar beyan olunduktan sonra

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gracious separation means inwardly distancing oneself and refusing to imitate wrongdoing, while not retaliating but responding with tolerance, forbearance, and good character.
rows.anchor: kalben ve fikren onlardan uzak durup fiillerinde onlara uymamakla beraber kötülüklerine karşılık vermeye kalkışmayıp müsamaha ve idare ve güzel ahlâk

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Some exegetes held that this gracious-separation command was revealed before the fighting command and later abrogated.
rows.anchor: Bir kısım müfessirler bu âyetin kıtal emrinden evvel nâzil olup sonra kıtal emriyle nesholunduğuna kāil olmuşlar.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Other exegetes say the command invokes God’s permission in matters more likely to secure acceptance and is not abrogated; Rāzī and the author judge this sounder.
rows.anchor: esah olan budur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet need not worry about affluent deniers: leave them to God and give them only a little respite, since God can fully deal with and punish them.
rows.anchor: Ve bana bırak o nimetler içinde zevk ederek yumuşak yaşamak isteyen refah sâhibi münkirleri ve mühlet ver onlara biraz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh chiefs were pleasure-loving people of wealth; the idiom “leave him to me” implies that the speaker will fully handle him.
rows.anchor: Kureyş’in sanâdîdi böyle idiler. Lisânımızda da mâlumdur ki “sen onu bana bırak” demek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keššāf distinguishes naʿma, naʿime, and nuʿma as luxuriating in blessing, benefaction, and joy, respectively.
rows.anchor: fethiyle “na‘me”, Fâtiha’da da geçtiği üzere “ni‘metle tena‘‘um” tereffüh, kesriyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choking food is identified with things such as zaqqūm, ghislīn, and darīʿ: it sticks in the throat and can neither be swallowed nor brought back up, alongside unbearable pain.
rows.anchor: boğaza duran bir taâm zakkum, gıslîn, darî‘gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have cried out when reciting this verse.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem bu âyeti okuyunca

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasan al-Baṣrī repeatedly set aside his ifṭār after recalling the choking-food verse, until Sābit al-Bunānī, Yazīd al-Ḍabbī, and Yaḥyā al-Bakkā persuaded him to drink barley-water.
rows.anchor: “yemeği kaldırın” dedi. İkinci akşam konuldu, yine hatırına geldi, yine “kaldırın” dedi.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī offers a spiritual reading of the four punishments: bodily attachments become shackles after death; frustrated desire burns as spiritual fire; deprivation is choking grief; and exclusion from divine illumination is the most painful torment.
rows.anchor: ‘Enkāl’ nefsin cismânî alâkalar ve bedenî lezzetler kaydında

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī cautions that the verses do not mean only spiritual punishments: both the four bodily torments as literal meanings and the four spiritual torments as familiar metaphors can be intended.
rows.anchor: ben âyetten murad yalnız bu rûhânî mânalardır demek istemiyorum.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supports the spiritual reading because the preceding discussion is not confined to bodily matters and grief and pain belong especially to the spirit, unlike an inanimate body.
rows.anchor: elem ü gussanın cismâniyetten ziyade rûhâniyet işi olmasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When earth and mountains shake, the mountains become flowing heaps of sand and the earth lies level; the upheaval especially signals the collapse of the powerful.
rows.anchor: bilhassa kodamanların yıkılacağına işaret vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After preparing the Prophet, the discourse turns to the deniers, including the Meccan polytheists, and announces that God sent them a Messenger to testify against their disbelief and rejection.
rows.anchor: Üzerinize şâhid kendisine karşı yaptıklarınıza şâhid olarak küfürlerinize, tekziblerinize

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with Moses and Pharaoh has three purposes: identify the promised end-time Messenger as Muhammad, liken Meccan polytheist rulers to Pharaoh in oppression, and warn that disobedience brings punishment.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ idi. Bu teşbihte üç mâna vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s disobedience to the Messenger ended in a grievous seizure, warning the audience to consider how they could escape if they disbelieve.
rows.anchor: Biz o Firavun’u vahim bir tutuşla tuttuk alıverdik Firavun öyle olunca

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day’s terror makes newborn children white-haired; the author also suggests it may indicate that enough time will pass for new generations to reach old age, with generations turning over.
rows.anchor: gam ve keder saçlar ağartır. Ma‘amâfîh bunda o

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky will split at the coming of that dreadful day, when divine command establishes a new world after the mountains melt and children age.
rows.anchor: yalnız dağlar erimek, çocuklar kocalmakla kalmayacak, o yüksek semâ bile yarılıp ayrılacak, emr-i ilâhî vârid olup yeni bir âlem kurulacak.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These warnings are a reminder and admonition; whoever wishes can take the path to God through faith, obedience, and good works, seeking safety and nearness to Him.
rows.anchor: dileyen Rabbine bir yol tutar o günün şiddet ve dehşetinden korunmak ve Rabbine selâmetle ermek için iman ve itaat ve hüsn-i amelle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon, night, and morning retain their ordinary meanings and display divine signs; they also evoke the rise of prophetic light amid the darkness of jāhiliyya, the night’s decline, and the approaching dawn of Islam, which is the passage’s main intent.
rows.anchor: Burada “Kamer”, “gece”, “sabah” kendi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seqar is one of the greatest calamities.
rows.anchor: her hâlde kübrâların birisidir. Yani en büyük beliyyelerin birisidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean that seqar warns humanity, or that it is a warning as to humanity; some attach it to the sura’s opening command to stand as a warner.
rows.anchor: İnzar etmek, gocundurmak itibariyle beşeri, yahut münzir olarak beşeri bunu bazıları sûrenin evveline merbut demişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each soul is held in pledge by its earnings and answerable before God; its felicity or ruin corresponds to its deeds, and good action can redeem it by repaying its obligations to God.
rows.anchor: Her nefis kazancına bağlıdır. Yani Allah indinde borçlu olarak kazancına rehindir. Saadet ve felâketi kazancıyla mütenâsibdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the right are excepted because some receive a greater share of divine grace than their works merit; divine justice gives proportionate reward, while grace grants unequal destinies and honors.
rows.anchor: bunlar yalnız kendi kesblerine merhun kalmayarak takdîr-i ezelîde Allah teâlâ’nın mahza fazl u kereminden nasipleri, kısmetleri ziyade takdir edilmiş olan bahtiyarlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unearned distinctions such as human status, spiritual ranks, prophethood, and Muhammad’s preeminence are grants of grace and do not conflict with the rule that a person receives what they strive for, since what is beyond effort is not one’s due.
rows.anchor: başkası insanın kendi hakkı değil, mahz-ı fazldır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the exception is connected, these people of the right are a narrower, more distinguished group, like the foremost in Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa.
rows.anchor: burada “ashâb-ı yemîn”, Sûre-i Vâkı‘a’da geçen “ashâb-ı yemîn”den ehas, sâbikūn gibi mümtaz bir mânada demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Various transmitted interpretations identify the people of the right as angels, sincere believers, Muslim children, those placed on the right in the primordial covenant, or those created for Paradise in the divine covenant report.
rows.anchor: melâike, muhlis mü’minler, etfâl-i müslimîn, mîsâk-ı fıtratta sağ tarafta vâki‘olanlar

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: A report attributed to ʿAlī identifies the people of the right with Muslim children, who enter Paradise with their parents without having earned deeds.
rows.anchor: Etfâl-i müslimîn rivayeti Hazret-i Ali’den deniliyor.

rows.speaker: Allah
rows.claim: A sacred report says God created some for Paradise and others for Hell, regardless of concern; this is cited as one interpretation of the people of the right.
rows.anchor: şunları cennet için yarattım ehemmiyet vermem, şunları da cehennem için yarattım yine ehemmiyet vermem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception does not mean no one who earns deeds enters Paradise; it highlights people who enter through pure grace, without earned deeds or with blessings beyond their merit.
rows.anchor: bu istisnâ ehl-i kesb içinde cennete girecek yok demek değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One meaning of people of the right is those placed on the right in destiny and favored without any role for personal effort; prophethood itself is such a divine gift.
rows.anchor: Birincisi: Kaderde sağ tarafta vâki‘olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second meaning takes yamin as covenant: those who entered the primordial divine pact and remained faithful benefit from their own deeds and, beyond them, shared blessings and happiness.
rows.anchor: “Yemîn” ahd ve mîsak mânasına olmasıdır. Çünkü mîsâk-ı fıtrî ile ahd-i ilâhîye dâhil olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author analogizes covenantal believers to a society bound by contract: each person gains from others’ shared labor in addition to personal effort, whereas isolated labor yields less.
rows.anchor: cemiyet hâlinde çalışması arasındaki farktır. Zira cemiyetle yaşayanlar yalnız kendi kesblerinden değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who unite their souls and efforts in God’s path and face one qibla are people of the right, receiving special divine grace; isolated self-directed people remain alone with their earnings.
rows.anchor: aynı kıbleye müteveccih olarak yürüyen hâlis iman sâhipleri kendi kesblerine bağlanmakla kalmayıp fazl-ı ilâhîden müstesnâ bir surette nasip alan ashâb-ı yemîndirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the right are in gardens and ask one another about the criminals, or make inquiries about them.
rows.anchor: Mücrimlerin hâllerinden kendi aralarında konuşur, bahseder, birbirlerine sorar yahut sordururlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although their inquiry is said to be for rebuke and regret, the author prefers an initial investigation into the nature of the crimes and possibility of intercession, which better fits the following mention of intercession.
rows.anchor: şefaat imkânını taharrî için bir hasbihâl veya istintak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inquiry is narrated to expose why criminals are condemned and warn people that intercession cannot rescue those guilty of the listed crimes.
rows.anchor: mücrimlerin hâllerini ve mahkûmiyetlerinin sebeplerini sorup araştırarak hakkı tebeyyün ettirmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks the criminals directly, or through an intermediary, what offense caused them to enter seqar.
rows.anchor: Bu sual, ashâb-ı yemînin birbirlerine değil de mücrimlere bizzat veya bi’l-vâsıta sordukları sualdir.

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Keššāf argues the question is not the righteous asking one another: that construction would say “what put them in seqar”; the wording reports the question actually posed to the criminals.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf der ki: Bu, ashâb-ı yemînin birbirlerine suallerini beyan değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals confess four failures: they did not pray, feed the poor, refrain from vain company and pointless talk, or believe in the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: fakire yemek vermez, karnını doyurmak çaresini aramazdık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neglecting prayer and the poor and joining vain talk ultimately stem from disbelief; they persisted in it until death made the truth certain.
rows.anchor: Namaz kılmamanın, fukarâya bakmamanın, dalanlarla beraber dalıp gitmenin asıl sebebi de bu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession cannot benefit those who died in disbelief: they did no saving deeds, and even universal intercession cannot alter the truth of their earned punishment.
rows.anchor: kendilerini kurtaracak amel yapmamış oldukları gibi şefaatçilerin hepsi de şefaat edecek olsa fayda vermez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possibility of the people of the right interceding for them might have remained had the criminals not denied the truth and died in disbelief.
rows.anchor: tekzib etmeseler, küfre gitmeselerdi belki ashâb-ı yemînin onlara şefaati de mümkin olabilecekti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from the Qurʾānic reminder cannot help deniers escape the fate it warns about.
rows.anchor: Bu Kur’an’dan yüz çevirmekte, o yakīni ihtar ile edilen nasihatten kaçınmalarında kendileri için bir fayda mı var?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who flee the reminder resemble frightened wild donkeys fleeing a lion, or a hunting party.
rows.anchor: Ekser lügaviyyûn “kasvere” arslan demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaswara is explained as a harsh or coercive person from the root kasr, a fierce hunting party, or a lion; most lexicographers say lion, and the word is also said to be Abyssinian.
rows.anchor: “Kasvere” “kasr”dan müştak olarak zorlu, zorba demek gibi olup zorlu avcı alayı veya arslan mânalarına geldiği beyan olunuyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wild donkeys flee danger and may escape, but those who flee Qurʾānic counsel run from salvation and toward ruin.
rows.anchor: budalalar ise tehlikeden değil, halâstan, halâskârdan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand for separately distributed pages may mean each wants an individually addressed reminder and invitation, perhaps with personalized tasks or benefits, or each wants to be a prophet.
rows.anchor: her kişi kendisine ayrı ayrı dağıtılmış sahifeler hâlinde tezkire getirilmesini istiyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reject a general reminder and imagine that each deserves a separate message like an invitation to a feast, or a personal notice about duties and preparation.
rows.anchor: Umûmî bir tezkire ile iktifâ etmek istemiyor. Her biri ziyafete davet olunur gibi husûsî bir tezkire ile ayrıca davet olunmasını istiyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There will be no separate reminder for everyone, and even if there were, they would still not come; their real problem is that they do not fear the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Hayır, öyle şey yok herkes için ayrı bir tezkire, ayrı bir kitap gelmesine ihtimal yok, bununla beraber öyle de olsa yine gelmezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is a reminder; anyone who wishes may reflect on its meaning and act accordingly.
rows.anchor: Artık her kim isterse düşünsün mazmûnunu anlasın, îcâbına göre hareket etsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People do not remember unless God wills; He alone is worthy to be feared and to forgive, and no one else can protect or pardon.
rows.anchor: Azâbından korkulup korunulacak olan da O, mağfiret edecek de O’dur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear and love of God are the foundation of wisdom.
rows.anchor: Onun için her hikmetin başı Allah korkusu, Allah mahabbetidir.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
rows.claim: In a report from Anas, the Prophet recites the verse and conveys God’s words: He alone deserves fear, forbids associating another deity with Him, and forgives those who fear Him without associating partners.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem bu âyeti هُوَ أَهْلُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ وَأَهْلُ ٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ okudu da dedi ki

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Hasan
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī from Ḥasan says God would be ashamed to turn back raised hands without forgiveness; despite the angels’ objection, God declares Himself worthy of piety and forgiveness and pardons the supplicant.
rows.anchor: Hakîm-i Tirmizî Nevâdiru’l-Usûl’de Hazret-i Hasan’dan tahric ettiği bir hadiste demiştir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prays to be included among those God protects and forgives.
rows.anchor: Yâ Rab! Bu kulunu da o koruduğun, mağfiretine erdirdiğin kulların zümresine ilhak eyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening lā is not a negation of the oath: the author reads it as a denial followed by an oath, as in the idiom lā wallāh, and cites Imruʾ al-Qays as poetic evidence for that usage.
rows.anchor: Kasemi nefy değil, لا والله “hayır vallahi, yok vallahi, değil vallahi” gibi nefiyden sonra kasemdir.

rows.speaker: Cumhur
rows.claim: Most exegetes treat lā in such oath formulas as an added connective used only for emphasis, as in the oath over the stars’ settings.
rows.anchor: Cumhur, bu gibi لا’ların sıla, yani mücerred tekid için ilâve edilmiş, zâid olduğunu söyler

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhsharī says lā inserted before an oath within a sentence, as in 4:65, emphasizes the oath; similarly it intensifies knowledge in 57:29.
rows.anchor: kelâmın arasında olursa kasemi tekid için ziyade edilmiş sıladır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When lā begins a discourse, as here and in Sūrat al-Balad, it is negation rather than a connective, since an added connective occurs within a statement.
rows.anchor: kelâmın ibtidâsında vâki‘olduğu zaman sıla değil, nefiydir. Çünkü sıla kelâmın esnasında olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negating before the oath heightens its force: the truth is so momentous that even swearing cannot convey its full greatness, which itself reinforces the oath.
rows.anchor: Şu söyleyeceğim söz o kadar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say the emphatic negation means the truth is too evident to need an oath, or rejects opposing ideas that came before it.
rows.anchor: bazıları da kasemden evvel geçmiş olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also explains it as clearing the listener’s mind of all opposing ideas before presenting the sole truth to follow.
rows.anchor: şöyle demek olur: “Şimdi zihninden bütün muhalif fikirleri sil, söylenecek ve dinlenecek başka bir şey yok

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Turkish rendering “yo…” was chosen to evoke the several possible senses of lā.
rows.anchor: Biz meâlde bu “lâ”yı, bu mânalara temas edebilmek için “yo…” diye ifade etmeyi muvâfık gördük.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-qiyāma is the day of rising after death, preceded by death and destruction; the answer to the oath is omitted and supplied by the question about whether God can reassemble people, affirming resurrection.
rows.anchor: Kalkım gününe kasem ederim ki siz muhakkak ba‘solunacak, öldükten sonra kaldırılacaksınız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs lawwāma can mean a soul that reproaches others or one that recognizes its sins and regrets them; the latter meaning is more familiar.
rows.anchor: Bu da ya başkasını levm eden, pek kınayan nefis, yahut yaptığı günahların fenalığını anlayıp da kendini kınayan, pişman nefis demek olabilir. İkincisi daha mâruf ve meşhurdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul’s stages may be counted as seven—commanding, reproaching, tranquil, inspired, pure, content, and pleasing to God—each a station in spiritual discipline.
rows.anchor: Nefs-i emmâre, nefs-i levvâme, nefs-i mutmainne, nefs-i mülhime

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oaths emphasize the painful importance of remorse at resurrection, when every soul will regret its worldly neglect and wish it had done better.
rows.anchor: hatta her nefis kendisini levm edecek, dünyada yaptığı kusura pişman olacak, “daha iyi neye çalışmadım, daha güzel işler neye yapmadım” diye pişmanlık edecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdī b. Abī Rabīʿa, a neighbor of the Prophet and son-in-law of al-Akhnas b. Sharīq, asked when and how resurrection would happen, then said he would not believe even if he saw it and challenged the gathering of bones; the report says the Prophet prayed against his bad neighbor.
rows.anchor: Adî bir gün Resûlullah’a “Yâ Muhammed, bana o kıyamet gününden haber ver bakalım, o ne zaman ve nasıl olacak?” demişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jahl also mocked the claim that God would collect decayed bones and restore them to a new creation; the sūra is reported to have been revealed concerning one of these men.
rows.anchor: Ebû Cehil de: “Muhammed, Allah teâlâ’nın bu kemikleri çürüyüp dağıldıktan sonra toplayıp yeni bir hilkatle iade edeceğini mi zu‘mediyor?” demişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite these occasions of revelation, “the human” should be understood generally, not restricted to those men, since a revelation occasion does not require exclusive reference; it does not mean every person thinks this way.
rows.anchor: sebeb-i nüzul tahsis ve tâyini îcab etmeyeceğinden zâhiri vechile cinse mahmul olması doğrudur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balā affirms a preceding negative by reversing it—“yes, indeed”—whereas naʿam or lā can simply repeat the negative; here the implied answer is that God will certainly gather the bones.
rows.anchor: “belâ” denildiği zaman “evet geldi” denilmiş olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied verb “We gather” supplies the sense of balā, and “being able” grammatically describes the implied subject of that verb.
rows.anchor: mukabil بـَلٰى نَجْمَع demektir. {قَٰدِرِينَ} de mukadder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can restore not only large bones but every detail, down to the fingertips; their fine construction signals the remarkable subtlety of bodily creation.
rows.anchor: en ince teşkîlâtına varıncaya kadar hepsini, hatta gövdesinin, etrafının en ince uçları olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hands symbolize power and accomplish people’s most important work; fingers and fingertips carry that agency and astonishing touch sensitivity, so reconstructing them encompasses the works and artifacts produced by a person.
rows.anchor: Parmaklarda ve parmak uçlarında öyle acîb bir sanat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author illustrates fingertip sensitivity with a person distinguishing materials and sacks in a dark shop by tapping with a cane; tactile nerves register fine differences in vibration.
rows.anchor: Karanlık bir gecede meselâ bir kiler veya bir dükkânda gezinirken elinizdeki bir baston ile şuraya buraya dürttükçe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can gather all human characteristics in one cell, just as a tiny particle of the tailbone is said to contain the person’s features.
rows.anchor: bir zerre içinde bir insanın bütün hususiyetlerini toplar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebellious person denies resurrection because he wants to continue desires, sins, and pleasures indefinitely, preferring ongoing immorality to righteousness; his question about when the Day is comes mockingly.
rows.anchor: masiyetlerinden, lezzetlerinden ayrılmamasını, ileride onlara devam etmesini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When resurrection begins and signs of death and destruction appear, the denier awakens to the world collapsing around him and regrets his deeds, but belated remorse is useless.
rows.anchor: Lâkin sonra o kıyametin başlangıcı başladı mı gözü açılır, dünyanın her taraftan başına yıkılmakta
